capability: Normalize tree-transparent containment merges without weakening capability or authority history
searchEvidence: The exact reviewed PR 401 head 298fec58598c963ebb0affe990ad8a02417691b7 passes repository validation, while its GitHub merge commit 017d5390c56f7b66870a5df0bb981bd5ec37f7b1 fails only because diff-tree -m repeats the already-audited PR changes against the first parent.

Commit 017d5390 has exactly two parents; its complete tree 13ad6e9f8b09896ff68df783ce502aa366bde134 equals only second-parent 298fec58, first-parent 0328f550 is an ancestor of that second parent, and the complete 298fec58..017d5390 tree diff is empty.

scripts/validate_repository.py already owns immutable record and attestation history through _record_changed_in_commits_after; extending that owner is smaller and safer than a second checkpoint, record retirement, history rewrite, or merge-specific release bypass.
semanticOwner: scripts/validate_repository.py remains the only capability and external-authority history validator
terminalContract: When auditing whether an immutable record, attestation, or checkpoint path changed after its evidence commit, treat one merge node as a duplicate history edge only when it has exactly two parents, its complete Git tree equals exactly one parent tree, and the other parent is an ancestor of that tree-equivalent parent. Continue auditing every commit in both ancestry paths. Any distinct tree, octopus merge, non-contained parent, later mutation, changed-then-restored content, or Git inspection error remains fail-closed. No checkpoint, record, attestation, risk, owner, firmware, release, or path-coverage semantics change.

designReview.evidence: Independent R3 design review verified the exact 017d5390 topology and approved a helper limited to _record_changed_in_commits_after. It rejected the broader recovery-manifest design and required continued ancestry traversal plus negative coverage for distinct-tree, non-ancestor, octopus, true mutation, changed-then-restored, final-record, and attestation paths. No P0, P1, or P2 design finding remains.
